# Mental Lexicon

![](images/7-How%20do%20words%20get%20meaning_0.png)



* All of this information about words is stored in our mental  __lexicon\.__
  * Kind of like a dictionary
  * Contains information about:
    * pronunciation
    * meaning
    * related words
    * sentence use
  * Linked to other related words

# Learning a word’s meaning



* As we’ve seen\, by and large the meaning of a word is 100% arbitrary
  * There’s NO direct relation between the word itself and the concept it represents
  * Juliet: “What's in a name? That which we call a rose\, by any other name would smell as sweet\.”
    * Is there anything inherently “rose\-y” about the combination of sounds /r/ \+ /o/ \+ /z/?
    * Persian  _gol_ \, Maltese  _warda_ \, Slovene  _vrtnica_  _\, _ Indonesian  _bunga_  _ _  _mawar_

# But there are non-arbitrary words!



* Onomatopoeia
  * Animal sounds: “buzz”\, “meow”
  * Environmental noises: “trickle”\, “tinkle”\, “splash”

# A brief tangent



  * Even though onomatopoeia is rather non\-arbitrary\, we still find significant variation among the languages of the world
  * What sound does a dog make?
    * _bark_ \,  _woof_ \,  _ruff_ \,  _arf_ \,  _bow_   _wow_
    * Arabic:  _hau_  _ _  _hau_
    * Chinese:  _wow wow_
    * German:  _wuff_  _ _  _wuff_ \,  _wau_  _ _  _wau_
    * Greek:  _ghav_  _ _  _ghav_  _ _ \(\[γaβ γaβ\]\)
    * Korean:  _meong_  _ _  _meong_  _ _ \(\[mʌŋ mʌŋ\]\)

# Back on track!



* When it comes to words and meanings\, your book points out that many people believe that the words/language you have directly affects how you think about the world
* This is called the  __Sapir\-Whorf Hypothesis__ \, and it has two main forms:
  * __Hypothesis of Linguistic Determinism__  – a language’s structure determines how you think
    * “Language causes a particular cognitive structure”
  * __Hypothesis of Linguistic Relativity__  – a language’s structure influences how one thinks
    * “The world is differently experienced and conceived in different linguistic communities”

---


# Problems with this “hypothesis”



* Inability to express certain thoughts with language
  * If thought were determined by language\, then you would either be able to express these concepts as clearly as you think them or not be able to think them
* Ability to utter nonsensical sentences
  * Colorless green ideas sleep furiously\!
* Humans without language can still think
  * Genie\, for example
* Circular reasoning
  * Language influences thought or vice versa?
* The question of translatability
  * If language determines thought\, then presumably some concepts would only be understandable in the language in which they were first thought

# Colors


---


![](images/7-How%20do%20words%20get%20meaning_18.png)



* Subjects were shown three squares of blue arranged in a triad
* Task:  _Which of the bottom two squares is identical to the top square?_
* Russian speakers were able to identify squares as  _light blue \(_  _goluboj_  _\) _ and dark blue \( _sinij_  _\) _  _more quickly _ than English speakers with no interference
* What does this mean?
  * Russian speakers  __do__  think about these colors as differently as we think about blue and green\, hence the quicker reaction time _ _
